sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Wake County, North Carolina?
sections.html:
Wake County Tax Administration appraises real estate and personal property and also sends and collects the bills. Its help desk answers at 919-856-5400 and taxhelp@wake.gov.

The county bills for more than itself. By local agreement, Wake County bills and collects tax and various fees for the municipalities and special districts inside its borders, so a parcel inside a town sees a county charge and a town charge on one bill. The county tells residents to contact their town government with questions about how a town rate was set.

If your mortgage company pays the tax out of escrow, you will not be mailed a bill. The county encourages those owners to look their bill up online or call Tax Administration. That matters if you are selling: a closing attorney needs the actual figure for any unpaid year.

sections.h2: What county rate did Wake County adopt for Fiscal Year 2027?
sections.html:
The county's 2026 tax bill page says the Board of Commissioners voted on June 1 to adopt a $2.28 billion budget for Fiscal Year 2027, including a 2-cent property tax increase that raises the county rate to 53.71 cents. That is the county's own wording, and it applies to the county portion only.

The page adds that total bills also depend on the rate of the municipality or special district where the property sits. Wake County prints its own example on the page, saying the owner of a $450,000 home will see a $90 increase. Use that as the county's statement of the change, and ask Tax Administration for the figure that applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: When are Wake County property taxes due and when does interest start?
sections.html:
North Carolina taxes are due September 1, and the county says you avoid interest by paying in full by January 5. Interest starts January 6, at 2 percent for the first stretch and then three-fourths of one percent for each month or fraction of a month from February 1 until paid.

The county page offers more flexibility than many owners expect. Residents can make partial payments in any amount, as long as the balance is cleared by January 5, and no prior approval is needed for installments on a current bill. Each payment brings a statement showing the remaining balance. Tax Administration can also set up short-term payment plans, and it says the sooner you call, the better the options. Once a bill goes overdue, the office says it cannot assist.

The page also warns that state law permits past due taxes to be deducted from paychecks, bank accounts or rent.

  • Online payment options include ACH or eCheck, PayPal, Venmo, Apple Pay, Google Pay and major credit cards.
  • Escrowed mortgages: the lender pays, and you do not get a mailed bill.
  • Questions about a bill: 919-856-5400 or taxhelp@wake.gov.

sections.h2: How does the 2027 Wake County revaluation affect a sale?
sections.html:
Wake County's current revaluation took effect January 1, 2024, and the next takes effect January 1, 2027, with revaluations every two years after that. A house sold in 2027 will be taxed on a new value, which a buyer's agent and a cash buyer will both look at.

The county explains that a revaluation sets the tax value of land and buildings so each property reflects fair market value, meaning the most probable price in an open market. It works through four steps: neighborhooding, land and building pricing from sales data, field and office review, and notice of assessment with an appeal review. For the 2027 cycle the county says its parcels, about 460,000 of them, are grouped into 5,400 neighborhoods.

  • January 19, 2027: results presented to the Board of Commissioners.
  • By January 22, 2027: owners start receiving Notices of Assessed Value.
  • February 2027: commissioners appoint the Board of Equalization and Review.
  • April 30, 2027: the county's planned deadline to file an appeal.

These are the county's published targets, so confirm them with Tax Administration at 919-857-3800 or revaluation@wake.gov.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Wake County property value?
sections.html:
You appeal to the Wake County Board of Equalization and Review, which the county says is where taxpayers take informal and formal appeals. The county's revaluation page says value notices are mailed first, and taxpayers can then appeal.

State law gives the board's calendar: it first meets no earlier than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May. A taxpayer asks for a hearing before the board adjourns, and a board decision can be taken to the state Property Tax Commission with notice filed within 30 days after the decision was mailed. In a revaluation year the board finishes by December 1.

Gather sales of similar nearby houses and any inspection or repair estimates before you file. A house with condition problems is the case where an owner has the most to show. If you are selling quickly and the appeal will not finish before closing, talk to the closing attorney about how any later change will be handled between buyer and seller.

sections.h2: What property tax relief does Wake County offer?
sections.html:
Wake County points owners to three state programs: the Senior and Disabled program, tax deferment and the Disabled Veteran program. They serve residents who are 65 or older with low income, residents who are totally disabled with low income, and veterans with a total and permanent service-connected disability or an unmarried surviving spouse.

Under state law the Senior and Disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or half of the appraised value of the permanent residence, and the income limit printed by the Department of Revenue for 2026 is $38,800. The disabled veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit. A circuit breaker limits tax to 4.0 percent of income up to the limit and 5.0 percent above it, up to 150 percent of the limit, and unpaid amounts are deferred and become a lien.

The state deadline is June 1. For 2026 the county said late applications may be accepted for good cause through December 31, 2026, and it listed illness, a death in the immediate family, military deployment or a delayed disability certification as examples. Forgetting is not on that list.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Wake County property tax when you sell?
sections.html:
An unpaid bill follows the property. State law attaches the lien on the date the property is listed for the tax year, and enforcement can be a foreclosure action in the county where the property lies.

In a sale, the closing attorney asks Tax Administration for the current amount, and the tax is paid from your proceeds so the buyer receives the parcel clear. If you are behind and the house is in poor shape, a quick cash sale can pay the arrears at closing. Do not wait past the January 5 date if you can avoid it, since interest begins the next day.

For an inherited house where taxes went unpaid, call Tax Administration first. It can explain what is owed and what payment options remain before the bill goes overdue.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to pay Wake County property tax without interest?
faqs.a: January 5. Bills are due September 1, and the county says paying in full by January 5, 2027 avoids interest on the 2026 bills. Interest starts January 6.

faqs.q: Does Wake County let me pay property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says partial payments of any amount are accepted before the January 5 deadline, with no prior approval needed for installments on a current bill. Tax Administration can also arrange short-term plans if you call early.

faqs.q: When does the next Wake County revaluation take effect?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. The county's current revaluation was effective January 1, 2024, and it says future revaluations will take effect every two years.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Wake County tax bill?
faqs.a: Wake County Tax Administration at 919-856-5400 or taxhelp@wake.gov. For revaluation questions, the county lists 919-857-3800 and revaluation@wake.gov.

faqs.q: Is there property tax relief for older or disabled Wake County owners?
faqs.a: Yes, through three state programs administered locally: Senior and Disabled, Tax Deferment and Disabled Veteran. The state deadline is June 1, and the county's page lists the groups who may qualify.
